item.title: Iraq October Oil Output Jumps to Highest Since 2019, IEA Says
item.description: Iraq’s oil output surged in October and production in the United Arab Emirates held near the previous month’s high, as Gulf producers increased crude flows despite shipping disruptions caused by the Iran war, the International Energy Agency said.

item.title: Why a $2 Billion Law Firm Suddenly Collapsed
item.description: What Weil Gotshal’s collapse says about the frailty of big law.

item.title: Odd Lots: Why a $2 Billion Law Firm Suddenly Collapsed (Podcast)
item.description: At the end of October, seemingly overnight, a major law firm called Weil Gotshal announced it was winding down after a number of partners departed and talks of a merger with another firm failed. So how did a $2 billion big law firm collapse in the span of a few weeks? In 2015, Yale Law professor John Morley published a paper called "Why Law Firms Collapse," that now looks very prescient, with his idea of a “partner run," or the law firm version of a bank run. item.title: Global Oil Market Swings to Surplus on Gulf Exports, IEA Says
item.description: Global oil markets will swing to a supply surplus for the first time since the start of the Iran war as Persian Gulf exports recover despite the ongoing conflict, the International Energy Agency said.
